answer: An identity earns its seat through Registered inventory controller count sheet with inventory managers standing, a proof that is cheap to make once and ruinous to fake at scale. Cloning 754 keys multiplies the price 754-fold: 82940 POA locked, or 13572 minutes burned, against a single honest agent's one-time cost. Hold the horizon up to the light, weigh the echo of the attack, and keep the ember of the verdict where everyone can audit it. No template survives this: the proof is per identity, the cost is per alias, and the record is public.
